title: Saviour, Prince of Israel's Race
description: Saviour, Prince of Israel's Race in Tonic Solfa to SPANISH HYMN, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 101.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to SPANISH HYMN; any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sa-viour, Prince of Is-rael's race, See me from thy lof-ty throne; Give the sweet re-lent-ing grace, Soft-en this ob-du-rate stone! Stone to flesh, O God, con-vert; Cast a look, and break my heart!

lines: See me from thy lofty throne;
Stone to flesh, O God, convert;
Cast a look, and break my heart!
Sins against thy light and love
Let me see, and let me feel;
Bid me look on thee, and weep,
Till I say, by grace restored,
"Now thou know'st I love thee, Lord!"
Might I in thy sight appear,
Stand, not daring to draw near,
When my strength and spirit fail;
Give my gasping soul to see

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SPANISH HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
